searchText: Did we ever settle on specifically which EIP is going to be the one for history expiry: - https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4444 well known and has the correct branding, however, it is specified as a rolling window of 1 year which is not accurate for what we are about to do. - https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7639 is accurate in specifying what is happening with clients dropping history with Pectra. Anyone have opinions? <@199561711278227457> suggestion of what block number should be the drop-block for devnet-6? Or anyone else who cares fo weigh in. you can drop it now in geth using `geth --sepolia prune-history` it's in the last release the client should mostly work we have chosen these blocks as cutoff points: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/f0cdc40cebd3fcb26d21ced0f1093efd7a2c949f/eth/ethconfig/historymode.go#L81 for devnet-6, we could just use epoch 2048? (electra happened at 10) not sure if you want to use a epoch boundary or just some random block in that range though. <@755590043632140352> for your testing purposes. Am I correct to assume this should be announced more broadly to the CL teams for testing? There's no need, pandaops already runs CLs pointed at these ELs, so if those nodes don't break and can still process deposits we're good Perhaps just resyncing a couple

excerpts.content:
Did we ever settle on specifically which EIP is going to be the one for history expiry:

- https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4444 well known and has the correct branding, however, it is specified as a rolling window of 1 year which is not accurate for what we are about to do.
- https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7639 is accurate in specifying what is happening with clients dropping history with Pectra.

Anyone have opinions?
